summary: Broaden vector practice to cover bearings, resolving from a vertical reference, and complete vector answers for changing motion.

improvements.why: The current bank tests a quadrant-II angle but never asks for a bearing or for components when the angle is measured from the vertical; the learner's mechanics notes discuss both compass directions and resolving.
improvements.what: Add one exam-style Find item giving a displacement in $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}$ and asking for magnitude and three-figure bearing, with north as $+\mathbf{j}$ and east as $+\mathbf{i}$; add one item resolving a force at an angle west of north into signed components, with a sine/cosine-swap distractor. Use exact values where possible.

improvements.why: Existing numerical items ask only for the magnitude of velocity or acceleration, whereas the syllabus applies full vectors to motion in a plane.
improvements.what: Add one structured Find item requiring the complete constant velocity vector from two non-origin positions and then its speed and direction; add one Show that item requiring component-by-component subtraction of two velocity vectors over a stated time interval to prove a given acceleration vector, including a negative initial component.

improvements.why: The note names a vector diagram but never demonstrates head-to-tail construction or its relation to a component sum; Pearson explicitly permits a vector diagram for M1-2.1.
improvements.what: Add a short, original text walkthrough: draw the second arrow from the first arrow's head, draw the resultant from the first tail to the second head, and check its signed $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ components; distinguish this from adding arrow lengths.
